content: GTK3 gtk_window_present explicitly calls gtk_widget_show() when the window is hidden — presenting/focusing a window you just hid re-maps it. Any 'focus the panel' call that lands after a hide therefore resurrects a dismissed window. For a tray utility panel, gtk_window_set_skip_taskbar_hint, gtk_window_set_skip_pager_hint and a UTILITY type hint keep it out of the taskbar and workspace switcher; gtk_widget_hide_on_delete on delete-event is the idiom for hide-not-destroy so the toplevel survives a close button. Wayland ignores most positioning hints, so panel geometry cannot be a cross-display-server guarantee.
